scenario_goal: Add a public Schema.document_diff(left, right, *, include_unknown=False, ignore_fields=()) method to marshmallow. Given two documents (plain dicts or dumpable objects), it returns an ordered list of change records describing how to turn the left document into the right one. Each record has op in {add, remove, change}, a dotted/bracketed path (e.g. 'address.street', 'tags[1]', 'members[0].age'), and left/right values. The diff is driven by the schema's declared fields (not by raw value comparison): it recurses into Nested fields by their sub-schema and into List fields element-by-element, and it only reports fields the schema knows about unless include_unknown=True. ignore_fields drops named top-level (or nested) fields from the comparison. Identical documents yield an empty list. The success condition is that document_diff deterministically produces field-level add/remove/change records that respect schema declaration order, Nested/List recursion, and the two options, without changing any existing Schema behavior.
actors: A caller (application code) that owns a marshmallow Schema and two documents to compare
The Schema instance that drives field traversal and serialization order
The verifier that applies an agent patch and runs F2P/P2P behavioral tests
domain_objects: marshmallow.Schema and its ordered field set (fields dict)
Nested field (single and many=True) with its own sub-schema
List field whose inner field may be a Nested or scalar
Document: a dict or an object that can be dumped by the schema
workflow: Caller invokes schema.document_diff(left, right) with two documents
Each document is normalized to a dict via dump() if it is not already a dict
For every field declared in schema.fields (in declaration order): compare left[field] and right[field]
Scalar field: if values differ, emit change; if present only on one side, emit add/remove
Nested (single) field: recurse with the nested sub-schema, extending the path with the field name
Nested(many=True) field: recurse per element index, extending path with [i]
List field: compare element-by-element by position, recursing into elements when the inner field is Nested
Unknown keys (present in documents but not in schema): ignored unless include_unknown=True
Fields named in ignore_fields: skipped entirely
Return the ordered list of records
state_and_lifecycle: document_diff is stateless and pure: it reads two inputs and returns a list; it does not mutate the schema or documents
Path construction follows declaration order of fields, giving deterministic output ordering
Nested recursion uses the nested field's own schema.fields, not a generic value walk
include_unknown and ignore_fields only affect the diff view, never stored schema state
conflicts_failures_recovery: Wrong recursion target: treating a Nested(many=True) element as a field value instead of a document caused KeyError on integer index; must recurse via the nested schema per element
Declaration-order determinism: output must follow schema.fields order, not dict insertion order of inputs
Missing keys: a field absent on one side must become add/remove, not a change with a sentinel
Unknown fields must not leak into the diff unless explicitly requested
Existing public Schema API (dump, load, validate) must keep identical behavior; document_diff is additive
observable_outcomes: document_diff returns a list of {op, path, left, right} records
add/remove/change semantics are observable from the record op and path
Nested fields produce dotted paths; List positions produce [i] paths
include_unknown controls whether non-schema keys appear
ignore_fields removes named fields from the report
Identical inputs produce an empty list
No change to dump/load/validate output or signatures
verifier_behaviors: F2P: document_diff does not exist on baseline (AttributeError) so all 11 feature tests fail on NOP

F2P covers: scalar change, top-level add/remove, identical->empty, nested recursion, list index change, list add/remove, unknown-field policy, ignore_fields, List(Nested), Nested(many=True) add, and accepting objects via dump
P2P: 826 upstream regression tests (schema/serialization/deserialization/fields) must still pass after the change
reward is binary: 1 only when all F2P and all P2P pass; missing/skipped count as failure
task_difficulties: Model the diff as schema-driven, not value-driven: traverse schema.fields in declaration order and decide recursion vs scalar per field type, instead of generically walking dicts
Handle Nested(many=True) correctly: each element is a document compared by the nested sub-schema, and the path uses [i]; confusing it with a single nested value causes KeyError on integer keys
Define unambiguous add/remove/change semantics for missing keys and for List positions, and keep path formatting (dotted vs bracketed) consistent across nesting depths
Keep the option contract precise: include_unknown widens the view to non-schema keys, ignore_fields drops named fields, without leaking into stored state or breaking existing API
